title: Tobey Maguire Officiates Ex‑Wife Jennifer Meyer’s Star‑Studded Hawaii Wedding to Geoff Ogunlesi
body:
Los Angeles jeweler Jennifer Meyer exchanged vows with music‑industry executive Geoff Ogunlesi in a lavish ceremony on the Hawaiian island of Lanai on Saturday, while her former husband, actor Tobey Maguire, stepped behind the altar to officiate the nuptials. The surprise‑filled affair, staged at the Four Seasons Resort Lanai, marked the culmination of a romance that began publicly in August 2024, when the couple announced their engagement with a series of intimate photographs shared on social media.  

The setting was quintessentially romantic: a sun‑drenched garden overlooking the Pacific, swaying palm fronds, and a backdrop of turquoise water that framed the couple’s first kiss as husband and wife. Meyer, 39, wore a custom‑designed, vintage‑inspired gown featuring a delicate lace bodice and a sweeping train that trailed across the resort’s manicured lawns. Ogunlesi, 41, complemented her in a classic navy tuxedo with a subtle silk lapel, his smile reflecting both nerves and joy. The guest list blended Hollywood’s glitterati with music‑business insiders, including A‑list actors, producers, and record label executives, underscoring the couple’s cross‑industry appeal.  

Maguire’s role as officiant added an unexpected layer of intrigue to the event. The “Spider‑Man” star, who divorced Meyer in 2020 after a seven‑year marriage, has rarely appeared in public in a ceremonial capacity. In a brief remarks segment, he spoke warmly about the couple, noting that love “takes many forms” and that he was honored to witness his former wife’s happiness. His participation, which appeared to be a gesture of goodwill rather than a publicity stunt, was widely praised for its display of maturity and mutual respect—a narrative that contrasts sharply with the often‑tabloid‑driven portrayals of Hollywood breakups.  

Meyer, known for her eponymous jewelry line that has adorned red‑carpet icons such as Rihanna and Beyoncé, has cultivated a reputation for understated elegance both in her designs and personal style. Her marriage to Maguire, which began in 2014, produced two children and a shared public image of a low‑key, family‑first couple. Since their separation, Meyer has focused on expanding her brand and engaging in philanthropic efforts, particularly in arts education. Ogunlesi, meanwhile, has built a reputation as a savvy executive at Universal Music Group, overseeing several successful cross‑genre collaborations and championing emerging talent from Africa and Asia. Their partnership appears to blend creative entrepreneurship with a shared love of music and design, a synergy that was evident in the ceremony’s curated playlist—a mix of classic soul, contemporary R&B, and a surprise live performance by a Hawaiian ukulele quartet.  

Industry observers suggest that the union could have broader implications for both the fashion and music sectors. Meyer’s access to Ogunlesi’s network may open doors for collaborative product lines that fuse jewelry with music‑themed aesthetics, while Ogunlesi could leverage Meyer’s design sensibility to enhance branding for his roster of artists. Moreover, the high‑profile nature of the wedding—complete with celebrity guests and a former spouse officiating—reinforces the growing trend of blended families and amicable post‑divorce relationships in the public eye, potentially reshaping narratives around celebrity breakups.  

As the newlyweds embark on their married life, they are already hinting at future projects that blend their respective worlds. Sources close to the couple indicate plans for a limited‑edition jewelry collection inspired by African rhythms, slated for release early next year, and a charitable concert series that will benefit music education programs in underserved communities. Whether these ventures materialize or remain aspirational, the wedding has set a tone of collaboration and forward momentum for Meyer and Ogunlesi, promising a partnership that extends beyond the altar and into the realms of art, commerce, and philanthropy.
